background: A Virginia alum and 1986 champion as a Celtics reserve, Carlisle became a head coach in 2001 with Detroit (100-64, 2002 Coach of the Year), then Indiana (2003-07, 181-147, 61-win 2004 team), then Dallas (2008-21, 555-478, 2011 NBA champion), before returning to Indiana in 2021-22. He entered his second Pacers stint with an 836-689 career record and has since passed 1,000 regular-season wins (reached in 2025-26, pre-cutoff knowledge). After 25-57 and 35-47 rebuilding years, the Haliburton-led Pacers reached the 2024 East finals and the 2025 NBA Finals (lost Game 7 at OKC, Haliburton tearing his Achilles in that game). With Haliburton out for all of 2025-26 and Myles Turner gone to Milwaukee, Indiana fell to the bottom of the East (record unverified). He is president of the NBA Coaches Association and holds a multi-year extension signed in 2025. His current teams play the league's fastest, most egalitarian pass-heavy offense with a deep 10-11 man rotation and, since 2024-25, aggressive ball-pressure defense.

research_notes: LOW-COVERAGE PROFILE: the shared per-turn web-search cap was reached after a single Carlisle-specific search (career stints and conflicting career totals: 836-689 on his 2021 return; 943-828 through 2023-24). Season records 2021-22 through 2024-25 are from pre-cutoff knowledge and consistent with those totals (836+25+35+47 = 943 wins), but were not individually confirmed by a session URL. The 2025-26 record (26-56) is an UNVERIFIED ESTIMATE; only the Haliburton Achilles injury (June 2025) and Turner's departure are known with confidence. No 2026-27 record found. Scheme, rotation and end-game scores rest on pre-cutoff knowledge plus 2025 Finals coverage and Miami's 2025-26 emulation of the Pacers' system; dimensions with empty sources are capped at confidence <=0.3. The 1,000th-win milestone timing is pre-cutoff recollection, not verified here. Age computed from Oct 27, 1959 birth date.
